rows.question: What is a transmon qubit?
rows.answer: A transmon is a type of superconducting charge qubit designed to have reduced sensitivity to charge noise [2]. It is a special type of qubit with a shunted capacitor specifically designed to mitigate noise [1]. The name "transmon" is an abbreviation for "transmission line shunted plasma oscillation qubit" [2]. Its design is similar to the Cooper-pair box, but it achieves its reduced sensitivity by significantly increasing the ratio of Josephson energy to charging energy ($E_J/E_C \gg 1$) through shunting the Josephson junction with an additional large capacitor [3]. This increased ratio mitigates noise and makes the qubit's energy levels independent of the offset charge, thereby prolonging the dephasing time [3].

rows.question: What did Hopfield and Hinton each contribute to the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics?
rows.answer: John Hopfield contributed his work on physics-inspired Hopfield networks, while Geoffrey Hinton made foundational contributions to Boltzmann machines and deep learning [5]. They shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for "foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks" [1][4].
